pr_title: dbus: extend SocktBind{Allow|Deny}= with ip proto
pr_body:
Support filtering by ip protocol (L4) in SocketBind{Allow|Deny}= properties.

The signature of dbus methods must be finalized before new release is cut, hence reserve a parameter for ip protocol.
Implementation will follow.

Closes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/19891
pr_comments: but i guess my last point doesn't really matter, the PR is fully correct the way it is, and the type thing can be changed later, given that it now is just  matter of taste.

@poettering

Cool, I'll address https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/19942#discussion_r652150024 with the rest implementation.

issue_context.title: Add L4 protocol filtering for SocketBind{Allow|Deny}=
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`SocketBind{Allow|Deny}=` unit properties already support filtering by address family, port or port range.
Filtering by L4 protocol, e.g. TCP, UDP, DCCP prevents services from using illegitimate L4 protocol.
This addresses feature request by @topimiettinen https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17655#issuecomment-800001162

This should be merged before [v249](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/milestones/v249) is finalized: dbus API ought to stay immutable across releases.
The implementation is halfway done at the moment of filing the issue.
comments:
I think it's fine to do this change up until the final release, we don't have to keep the dbus api stable before then.

Currently the filters are described as `"a(iqq)"`. I guess something like `"a(iiqq)"` will be appropriate. If we don't manage to get the implementation done quickly enough, I think we should merge a simple patch which adds the additional param, but requires it to be 0 on input, and always outputs 0 in output. We can then add other values in a backwards-compatible fashion.

review_comments: for the time being, please add an if check that refues ip_protocol != 0

ah, uh. libc uses "int" for both these things, see socket() prototype, hence I actually think we should use `int` to wherever we can. However there's one place where we shouldn't: when passing a pointer to these field to sd_bus_message_read(), because theoretically int and int32_t might be two different things...

hence, please continue to use `int` here. However, when invoking sd_bus_message_read() pass pointers to true int32_t variables, and then assign from there to the `int` fields the value sactually should end up in.

i.e. the mess around in32_t vs. int should remain specific to sd_bus_message_read()/D-Bus, which causes it. Once we got our data out of that, let's not leak the type confusion and let's use libc's preferred type for this everywhere else, i.e. `int`, if you follow what i mean
